Container.Name: hikari-index-analyze
Container.Overview:
The analyze worker for Hikari Index, on CPU: it describes each frame (tags, faces, shot size, camera angle, similarity) and picks the stills. Install "hikari-index" first and start it once; this container then finds its token in that container's Config folder, so there is nothing to paste.
It is the heavy part: a large image (about 3.5 GB to download) and, while it works, about 1 GB of memory and every CPU core you leave it, for roughly ten to fifteen minutes an episode on four cores. Pin it to a few cores if the server has other work. It waits quietly when there is nothing to do.
Container.Requires: hikari-index, started once. Use the same version of both. Extra Parameters runs this container as user 99:100, the hikari-index template's PUID and PGID; if you changed those, change --user here to match.

Config.Name: Gallery
Config.Description: Where this container reaches the gallery. The default is this server, seen from a bridge container, on the gallery's usual port; change the port if you changed the gallery's Web port. If this container's log says the gallery is not reachable, put the server's own address here instead, for example http://192.168.1.10:5183.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: The same folder as the hikari-index container's Data. Read-only.

Config.Name: Standby
Config.Description: Optional. 1 makes this worker a fallback: it takes work only when no regular analyze worker (a GPU machine, say) has checked in for ten minutes.

Config.Name: Check for work every
Config.Description: How often it asks for work when it has none, in seconds.

Config.Name: Token folder
Config.Description: The worker-tokens folder inside the hikari-index container's Config folder.

Config.Name: Worker name
Config.Description: The name the token belongs to. Leave it.
